title: Polylang async invoker shims for streamed structured events
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: implement lightweight, language-specific shim libraries (TS/Py/Go) that present a single async invoker contract for streaming model responses + tool/function calling, emitting typed structured-event envelopes and providing backpressure-aware handlers. Motivation: customers building multi-language microservices need consistent semantics for streaming + tool calls so that rollouts and SDK examples can be shared across platforms without rewrites. Scope: - Define event envelope v2 (metadata, kind, id, payload, schema_version). - Implement shims that translate runtime streaming frames into the envelope and expose an async iterator / channel / callback API per language. - Provide canonical examples for function/tool calls and structured output parsing. Non-goals: replacing existing higher-level SDK surfaces, adding new transport protocols (work uses existing HTTP/HTTP2+streams), or changes to server-side API surface beyond metadata field additions (already planned in API team).
acceptance_criteria: A language-agnostic event envelope v2 is published and documented on Confluence
TypeScript, Python, and Go shim packages implement the same high-level API (async iterator / channel / subscription) and pass the shared conformance tests
Examples for: streaming chat + tool call -> structured output (JSON schema) and streaming embedding/partial results are live in the SDK examples repo
Integration test with runtime shows correct KV cache headers propagated and streaming reconnect + resume works under dropped-connection scenarios
Performance: per-request median latency overhead of shim layer < 1ms on benchmark harness (1000 reqs)
technical_notes: Event envelope v2 fields: id, timestamp_iso, kind: (token|delta|tool_invocation|tool_result|meta), payload (string or JSON), schema_version: 'v2', origin: (client|runtime|tool)

Backpressure model: TypeScript uses AsyncGenerator with manual pull; Python exposes an AsyncIterator with a .pause()/.resume(); Go uses a buffered channel with configurable buffer and a non-blocking DropPolicy and a blocking BlockPolicy option for high-SLO routes
Compatibility layer: shim packages implement a thin codec that maps runtime frames (raw bytes / JSON fragments) into envelopes and exposes both raw-frame and typed-envelope APIs for power users
Schema validation: use existing evals schemas for structured output; shims should include optional runtime validation with pluggable validator hooks
Security: shims must preserve token headers and not log payloads by default; follow SDK logging policy
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal devs + two early customers (private beta) for TS and Py (2 weeks)
Beta: add Go shim and expand to 10 customers; gather perf and error telemetry (3 weeks)
GA: publish packages to npm/pypi/godoc with migration guide and sample apps (1 week after beta sign-off)
testing_plan: Unit tests: envelope encode/decode, edge cases (partial JSON chunks, unexpected frames)
Conformance suite: shared tests in sdk-examples that run against all three language shims
Integration: run against runtime staging with simulated packet loss and latency profiles
Load: 1000 concurrent streaming sessions, confirm median shim latency < 1ms overhead
qa_steps: Smoke: run sample chat + tool call in each language and assert final structured output meets schema
Manual: review logs for dropped frames and reconnect attempts; confirm no PII leaked in debug logs
Security: ensure SDK packages set minimal default permissions and do not auto-send telemetry without consent
implementation_notes: TS: build on top of existing fetch + ReadableStream helper in runtime client. Provide both promise-based stream consumption and a pull-based AsyncGenerator example.
Py: leverage anyio/asyncio streams; provide compatibility shim for sync callers via a blocking wrapper that yields structured events synchronously.
Go: keep channel sizes configurable; expose Context-aware APIs for cancellation and deadline propagation.
Conformance harness: single repo 'sdk-examples/conformance' with test vectors and golden JSON outputs; CI job to run these against PRs to ts-shims/py-shims/go-shims
